status: Research ongoing. The universal target is unproved in this run.
new_auxiliary_definitions: The new Lean modules introduce auxiliary losses, gates, tropical scores, and orthant signs. No original model definition or target statement was weakened. ConditionalFractionCompletion adds completionPairing, StrictFractionCompletion, and PositiveSlackFractionCompletion, with the residual held fixed.

lean_results.scope: A fixed denominator list whose numerator span meets every strict orthant must have at least (2^n-1)/n heads. Target-dependent denominator lists are not excluded.

In every dimension and on every nonempty finite coordinate face, bounds the alternating sum of an affine fraction with positive constant term and nonnegative slopes by its range. Arbitrary unbounded coefficients prevent a universal head lower bound from this alone.
Strict tropical winning inequalities imply an ordinary real rational sign representation at a sufficiently large finite base. Existence of such winners for all truth tables is not proved.
For the two-bit parity labeling, positive affine-denominator one-head hinge losses have unattained infimum two. This invalidates an unqualified minimizer-existence step.
A particular fixed Cauchy codebook cannot contain repeated prescribed valleys. Adaptive general denominators are not excluded.
An exact finite Boolean corner identity using six fractions. No asymptotically efficient universal composition follows.
An exact finite Boolean corner identity using eight fractions. No asymptotically efficient universal composition follows.
A restricted constant-numerator tropical ansatz needs a binomial number of heads for a prescribed adjacent-layer flip. This is not a lower bound for the full model.
A finite set with injective coordinate ranks in a small summed-rank-distance ball has bounded cardinality.
Dominance in a positive two-vector combination forces common coordinate signs on the dominating vector. This is an algebraic lemma, not the full matching obstruction.
Exact orthant sign orthogonality and second moments bound the fraction of exceptional orthants for a fixed vector.

An explicit denominator-only quadratic penalty gives an attained positive two-bit parity hinge minimum of 13/4 at admissible positive slopes. The minimizer has hinge kinks; regularization alone does not repair the smooth-minimum argument.

After clearing positive denominators, an increasing codebook with all 2^r distinct strict polynomial sign words of degree at most H satisfies 2^r <= r*H+1. The rational clearing step is given in the manual audit; the Lean theorem states its polynomial hypotheses explicitly.

For a fixed residual and one denominator orientation, strict one-head completion is equivalent to normalized linear feasibility with positive common slack. A nonnegative moment witness certifies noncompletion of that residual. Neither result proves universal feasibility or progress.

manual_results: Parameter and fixed-denominator barriers distinguish exact real-table interpolation from target-dependent Boolean sign interpolation.
A multidegree count yields a full-model asymptotic lower bound with constant one, not the desired upper bound.

Universal compressed families cannot use only a low-dimensional denominator direction space, common scalar statistic, polynomial-degree moment curve, or uniformly mild conditioning and relative margin.
A family with H <= C*2^n/n^2 whose denominator slopes use K projective directions has at most 2^(n^2*K+O_C(2^n*log(n)/n)) strict sign patterns. Thus universality requires K >= (1-o(1))*2^n/n^2.
Quadratic curvature features span all tables with O(2^n/n^2) base denominators, but this does not supply score representations with that many heads.

Independent spherical and logarithmic-scale random span dictionaries have vanishing expected matched fraction in a fixed orthant at exponential dictionary size. These probability statements do not exclude rare or correlated deterministic constructions.

For r=2^k, k>=3, an unconditional binary-addressed scalar decoder uses at most 2^(r+1)/r+4*r-3 positive affine-pole fractions. It follows from a full self-dual necklace enumeration with few track transitions. The scalar encoder is not supplied.
Every scalar-code decoder with r output bits and H affine fractions per bit satisfies r*H>=2^r-1 if it realizes all words. Thus the new scalar decoder has optimal order on the stated sequence of r.

The explicit composition 1/(1+1/(1+x+2*y)+1/(1+2*x+y)) has an irreducible quadratic pole, so no finite sum of affine fractions equals it as a rational identity. This is not a Boolean sign lower bound.

A convex piecewise-linear surrogate for a single-head rational hinge update gives an explicit positive step with strict actual loss decrease whenever the surrogate improves. The proof includes hinge kinks and preserves denominator admissibility. No global progress or head-count theorem follows.

For every positive affine denominator, in any dimension, the absolute full-cube alternating sum of A/B is at most its range. A positive weighted edge-difference identity proves the sharp constant one. Consequently every unit-margin parity representation has total head range at least 2^n, independently of head count.

A downward radius-one covering code gives an explicit positive-slope full-cube representation with margin at least 3/4, using Mobius coefficients and epsilon=1/(4*n*3^n). This is an O(2^n/n) initialization only. A fixed number of heads cannot shatter all labelings of a radius-two Hamming ball, by a local Warren count.

Two positive-slope representations on opposite cube faces can be glued with the sum of their head counts, using explicit scale separation. Thus W_+(n)<=2^(n-m)*W_+(m). A target-rate positive-slope bound on power-of-two dimensions would extend to all positive dimensions with a factor four; that antecedent remains unproved. This statement does not assume that mixed-orientation scores can be glued at the same cost.

For a fixed residual score and one denominator orientation, strict completion by one head is equivalent to a linear program having positive common slack. Prescribed single-head margin superlevel sets are convex. No coupled-head progress theorem follows.

For N polynomial score coordinates of degree at most d in p<=N parameters, universal strict-sign coverage requires d>=(p/(4*e*N))*2^(N/p); an M-chart union has exponent (N-log2(M))/p. Fixed-base bounded-order perturbations at the target head budget therefore cannot be universal.

The entire largest-denominator-term proxy with arbitrary affine numerators and both uniform orientations has at most [2*(n+1)!]^H*(8*e*2^n/p)^p strict sign tables, p=1+2*H*(n+1)<=2^n. It cannot be universal at O(2^n/n^2) heads, and almost every function needs at least (1-o(1))*2^n/(n*log2(n)) proxy heads. This includes the unit-gap dominant-power certificate family, but is not a lower bound for full affine denominator sums.

blocked_routes.gap: Paired-head perturbations do not preserve pairing. Smooth hinge arguments do not cover kink minima or nonattainment. A denominator-only regularizer can ensure an attained positive minimum at hinge kinks, as formalized in RegularizedParityHinge. The unpenalized fixed-denominator refit succeeds on one saved example and fails on others. Fixed-base polynomial perturbation charts of degree polynomial in n cannot provide universal sign coverage at the target head budget, even when their separate features span all tables. Continuously varying base denominators or sufficiently high-order effects are not excluded.

The new single-track construction resolves binary addressing for a freely supplied scalar code. It does not supply an affine encoder for independently chosen words at all cube inputs. Raw composition with sums of heads can create irreducible poles; an admissible sign-preserving compiler remains missing.
CRT and digit encodings require an admissible single-layer decoder. Floor, residue extraction, multiplication, and added depth cannot be treated as free.

Explicit switching identities do not yield n-squared bits of independently programmable local capacity at constant head cost. Radius-two asymmetric covers have the desired number of cells, but the local constant-head compiler is impossible by a Warren count. Globally interacting heads are not excluded.

Closed at the target order: every unit-gap dominant-power certificate lifts with the same signs to a largest-term denominator proxy. Counting all coefficient orders, orientations, and arbitrary affine numerators bounds proxy coverage by 2^o(2^n) at H=O(2^n/n^2). Reopening requires using full denominator sums or cancellations outside that certificate condition.
Several independent random and structured dictionaries are obstructed. A correlated dictionary with all required matchings and admissible affine addressing has not been supplied.
Counting many sign patterns, complex closure results, and lower bounds do not establish coverage of every Boolean labeling.

remaining_target: Prove, without modifying the manuscript model, that a single absolute C gives W(n)<=C*2^n/n^2 for every positive integer n. No complete construction or existence proof is claimed.
